  "text": "The first thing Ellen unpacked was the kettle. The second was a blue cup with a chip she always turned towards the wall.

Outside the kitchen window, someone had left three empty pots along the fence. Each contained a label for a plant that was no longer there.

She was filling the kettle when the doorbell rang.

A man in slippers stood on the step, holding a small parcel.

“This came to ours.”

The name on it was her husband's.

“That's right,” she said.

The man glanced past her at the boxes.

“Getting settled?”

“More or less.”

After he left, she put the parcel beside the sink. Paul had ordered things weeks ahead: light bulbs, envelopes, a replacement part for something he hadn't yet taken apart.

She found scissors in a box marked BEDROOM.

Inside the parcel were six wooden plant labels and a pencil. Nothing else. She checked beneath the folded packing paper.

The kettle clicked off.

They had seen the house in February. Paul had stood at the kitchen window while the agent explained the boiler warranty.

“You could grow beans there,” he'd said afterwards.

“You could,” she'd told him.

Ellen made her tea. Then she went outside and tipped the old soil from one pot. A snail clung to the drainage hole. She eased it free with a label and set it beneath the fence.

There was no compost, and she didn't know whether it was too late for beans.

She brought the pot to the back door, where she would see it, and went to look for a pen to start a shopping list."
